writeup: TIC 367157113 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.457953 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 2.54% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal reached a detection significance of 1940.3 in the BLS periodogram, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.0, though the centroid offset of 1.2 arcsec from the target warrants note. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, the eclipse depths show significant alternating variations, indicating the true period is double the initially measured value. The pipeline's machine-learning model assigns this target a score of 0.49, reflecting moderate confidence in its physical reality.
